transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I’m here because I’m tired of avoiding things. I keep staying away from my workshop, and I skip family get-togethers if there’s a chance my brother-in-law will be there. After all this time, I’m just worn out from planning my life around not running into those reminders.
Do you ever experience sudden episodes of intense fear or discomfort?
I don’t think so, no. I mean, I get uncomfortable around certain reminders, but I wouldn’t call it sudden intense fear like an attack or anything.
Can you tell me more about what specifically makes you want to avoid your workshop or certain family gatherings?

It’s mainly the reminders. My workshop used to be my place, but now I find myself staying away from it because being in there brings things up I don’t want to deal with. And with family gatherings, if I know my brother-in-law might be there, I’ll usually skip it. I’ve just gotten tired of arranging everything around avoiding those situations.
What are these reminders that you're trying to avoid?

Mostly it’s my workshop, and then seeing—or even thinking I might see—my brother-in-law at family gatherings. Those things just bring it all back enough that I’d rather steer clear. I’ve been planning around avoiding them for a long time, and I’m tired of living that way.
What happened that makes your workshop and your brother-in-law reminders you want to avoid?

Well… it’s those places and people that bring it back for me. My workshop used to be just mine, you know, but now I avoid it. And if there’s a family get-together where my brother-in-law might be there, I usually don’t go. I came in because I’m tired of planning my whole life around not running into those reminders.
What happened involving your brother-in-law that you're trying to avoid reminders of?

I keep seeing this image of his hand holding that heavy tool. It comes out of nowhere, like when I’m shaving or even just working on a painting, and my chest tightens up. That’s the part I keep trying not to be reminded of.
What happened with your brother-in-law and the heavy tool that you're trying not to think about?

I remember the shouting, and I remember seeing that heavy tool in his hand. That part is clear enough. But right around how it actually ended… there’s just a blank spot. Like a few minutes are missing, and I can’t make them come back.
What do you think might have happened during the time that you can't remember?

I don’t really know. That’s the problem. I remember the shouting, and I remember him with that tool in his hand, clear as anything. But right around how it ended… it’s just gone. Like a few minutes got cut out and I can’t get them back.
Did the incident with your brother-in-law and the heavy tool involve any physical harm to you or someone else?
I’m not sure. I don’t remember that part clearly enough to say. I know there was shouting, and I saw the tool in his hand, but whether anyone was actually hurt… I just can’t tell you for certain.
Do you think the incident with your brother-in-law and the heavy tool was traumatic for you?

Yes… I think it was. Even if I can’t remember all of it, it still comes back to me. Out of nowhere I’ll see his hand holding that heavy tool, like a picture popping into my head, when I’m shaving or working on a painting. And when it happens, my chest tightens up.
For how long have you been avoiding your workshop and family gatherings where your brother-in-law might be present?
Since that confrontation with my brother-in-law… so, about two years and four months now. That’s when I started staying away from the workshop and from gatherings where he might be there.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself when these memories or reminders come up?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get shaken up when it comes back to me, but I haven’t noticed feeling like I’m outside my body watching it happen.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving the confrontation with your brother-in-law when the memories or reminders come up?

Not exactly like I’m back there living it all over again. It’s more like a sudden picture in my mind—his hand with that heavy tool—and it can happen when I’m shaving or painting. When it comes up, my chest tightens and I feel shaken.
Do you ever feel numb or disconnected from yourself or the world around you when you're reminded of the confrontation with your brother-in-law?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I feel numb, exactly, or disconnected from everything. I mostly just know I get upset when it comes up, but that “not feeling real” kind of thing… I haven’t noticed that.
Do you ever feel like you're back in the moment of the confrontation with your brother-in-law, reliving it as if it's happening all over again?

No, I wouldn’t say it feels like I’m back there and it’s happening all over again. It’s more like, out of nowhere, I see his hand with that heavy tool in my mind, like a picture popping up. It can happen when I’m shaving or working on a painting, and my chest tightens when it does.
Do you try to push away or avoid thoughts or memories of the confrontation with your brother-in-law when they come up?

Yes. I try not to think about it, and I end up avoiding things that bring it up. I don’t go out to my workshop much anymore, and I steer clear of family get-togethers if there’s a chance my brother-in-law will be there. I’m just tired of arranging my life around not running into those reminders.
Do you ever feel like things aren't real or like you're in a dream when you're reminded of the confrontation with your brother-in-law?
No, I don’t think so. I get bothered by it, but I don’t feel like I’m in a dream or that things aren’t real. I haven’t noticed anything like that.
Do you ever feel like you're detached from yourself when reminded of the confrontation with your brother-in-law?

No, I don’t think I feel detached from myself. I get upset when something reminds me of it, but I still feel like me, if that makes sense. I haven’t noticed anything like watching myself from the outside.
